entries.name: Confirm sheet by risk
entries.summary: A dialog for a change that has consequences: the plan in order with before and after, what it needs and holds, how to undo it; for the dangerous ones a typed word that seals it.

When it starts the sheet can fly into a tray. Failed and finished changes have a result sheet each. entries.name: Timed reveal
entries.summary: A sealed card with a draining ring; open it and each value shows in place of its button for a short time, then hides itself; closing hides all of them at once.

Each row has its label and key (edit.locked in the mono face), the help, and a meta line: the layer that enforces it with a page or database glyph (Enforced by the page, Enforced by the database rule, from level), Changed by who and when, and, when the value differs from its default, the default itself beside a gold diamond on the label, so the word says it and not the colour. A row saves at once through config.set and says Saved with a check, or the rejection with a cross, in its own status line; Undo restores the previous value for ten seconds. Without user.canEdit every control is disabled and the summary says so. A proposal whose base version is no longer live is classified against the live record, not refused. Per proposal: the summary, who, when and the status (merged reads 'merged, not yet published'); each part opens to a line diff of its live html against the proposed html; each held item shows the base, live and proposed hashes and both versions, and editors pick Keep live or Take the proposal, which is written on the proposal as a decision. The files it will publish are listed with their ifMatch. Apply is off until every held item is picked; presses within the debounce window fold into one artifact.publish files-form call with an ifMatch per file; after {shas} it writes manifest/current (the new hashes, the next seq and the version), parts/<id>, content/<id>, changes/<seq> with from and to hashes, and sets the proposal applied. On a conflict it names the files that moved (expected and actual sha), records the conflict and leaves the proposal held. Decline asks for a reason inline and records it. The presence line says who is watching when a presence/* doc is fresher than assist.presence-minutes, else offers the handoff 'watch the artifact <url>' with the open request ids and a copy button. Under them a version line puts every version on a track in order (spaced evenly, not to a time scale): the chosen span is drawn heavy, the two ends are rings, and data changes are small diamonds between the versions they fall between. A tally follows (added, removed, changed and data changes, each a count with its mark and word); the same sentence goes to a role=status line for screen readers. Then one panel with four lists. A changed part shows its id, the first eight characters of its from and to hash, and every change between the two versions that touched it, with who and when. entries.name: Request card
entries.summary: One request to Claude as its sender follows it: kind, block, a four-station track from queued to done, the conversation with Claude's answer, progress lines, the blocks it changed, and a reply box.

source.what: the lane eyebrow, the state pill, the four-segment track, the thread, the progress log, the changed chips, the reply box

changed: The track is one seam with a word under every station; the source coloured four segments.
Replies are append-only turns read through the engine; the source rewrote the whole turns list.
A stuck request says that nothing failed and what it waits for.
The header lists the kinds a session answers: task, fix, design note.
entries.about: Kit.requestCard.mount(box, {engine, rid}) follows one request through the assist engine (engine.thread and engine.reply); mount(box, {request, thread, onReply}) draws the same card from data. The header says what kind of request it is (task, fix, design note) with a glyph, which block it is about (a button that shows the block when onReveal is given) and when it was sent. The track is four stations on one seam: queued, seen, working, done; passed segments fill in the seam colour, the current station has its bead and its word in bold, and the word sits under every bead, so the state never rides on colour. A request queued for more than three minutes says it is still queued and that nothing failed. Below: the conversation in order (the person's words, Claude's answer in Markdown when kit.md and its libraries are loaded, plain paragraphs otherwise, then every reply), the block as it was sent, the session's progress lines with their times (open while it works), and the blocks it changed. Once Claude has answered, a reply box appears; Ctrl or Cmd + Enter sends, the reply reopens the request, and a draft survives a redraw. When sending is not available to the viewer it says so instead. Changes of state are announced. At 390 px the header wraps and the track keeps its four stations.

config: engine and rid (live), or request {id, lane, scope, text, quote, by, at, status, state, ackBy, progress, response, changed, version} and thread {text, response, turns} (static); me, names {uid: name}, titles, onReveal(partId), onReply(rid, text) for the static form, canReply, markdown(text), now, words; returns {update, destroy}
optional: a Kit.assist engine (pattern.assist); the card reads engine.thread(rid) and writes only through engine.reply

db.note: none directly; with an engine, the engine reads requests/<rid> and its turns and writes the reply

entries.name: Session presence
entries.summary: Whether a Claude Code session is watching the artifact, a Ping that proves it with the time it took, and the nudge that says how to start one: tell Claude Code to watch the artifact, with a Copy button.

source.file: a drafting board's session line, Ping button and panel
source.what: watching within five minutes, busy with what, the ping states and its 90 s timeout
the copyable watch the artifact line

changed: One view with a compact form for a panel header.
The nudge says requests queue only when they can; the source always said so.
The line says a session is woken when you send a request, when the platform reports a watching session and no presence doc is fresh.
entries.about: Kit.presence.mount(box, {engine, artifactUrl}) reads engine.presence() and draws one line: a bead, a word (a session is watching, a session is working, no session is watching) and a sentence (which session, when it was last seen, what it is doing). Ping calls engine.ping(); while it waits a count shows the seconds, and the result says the session answered in 1.1 s or that no answer came (the engine waits 90 seconds). When nobody watches or a ping times out, the nudge says to open Claude Code and tell it watch the artifact <link>, with a Copy button; when the clipboard refuses, the line is selected so it can be copied by hand. It says requests wait in the queue only while sending is available, and that Ask now needs no session when the page can ask. compact: true keeps the line for a panel header and puts the nudge behind How to start one. Without an engine, pass presence and onPing. The state is never colour alone; the ping's start and end are announced. At 390 px the buttons drop under the line.

config: engine (live) or presence {watching, busy, sessions [{session, at, doing}]} and onPing() -> 'pong' | 'timeout'; artifactUrl, compact, canPing, ask, queued, now, words; returns {update, ping, destroy}

db.note: none directly; with an engine, the engine reads presence/<session> and sends the ping request

entries.name: Assist panel
entries.summary: The page's lane to Claude in one panel: whether a session watches, a composer (kind, block, words) that sends to a session or asks Claude at once, and the feed of request cards or the current conversation.

source.what: the mode switch, the kept draft, the byte count, Ctrl+Enter, the reason line
open or all requests, the session line and Ping above them

changed: Ask now (an immediate answer) and the session lanes share one composer; the source had a separate bar per lane.
The request is about a picked block with its quote, not the button that was pressed.
A send that is not possible says why and keeps the words; with no way at all, Copy for Claude.
entries.about: Kit.assistPanel.mount(box, {engine, titles, onReveal, artifactUrl}) builds over the assist engine only. At the top, the presence line (compact). The composer: what kind of request, as radio buttons with one line on what each does (Ask now answers here and changes nothing; Task, Fix and Design note go to a Claude Code session), which block it is about (Pick a block or the shortcut, then the block's name, id and quoted text with Change and Clear; without a block it is about the whole page), the words, and Send, whose label says where it goes. Ctrl or Cmd + Enter sends. When a way is not available the composer says why in words (only editors can send, no session is listening, sending is off, Ask now is not available) and keeps the draft, which also survives a reload; with neither way, Copy for Claude puts the block and the words on the clipboard. The feed shows the requests as request cards, newest first (all, or open only), so an answer stays in view when it lands, or the conversation, where Claude's answer streams in as it is written, earlier conversations can be continued, and a question can be sent on to a session as a task. Start the engine with onPick: p => panel.setScope(p, true) so the shortcut fills the composer. Everything is reachable from the keyboard in reading order, and sends, answers and errors are announced. At 390 px the kinds sit two by two and the buttons go full width.

config: engine (a Kit.assist engine, required), lanes, project, titles, onReveal(partId), artifactUrl, me, names, shortcut, words {title, kind, lanes, help, send}; returns {setScope, pick, show, focus, destroy}
onPick: p => panel.setScope(p, true), so the shortcut fills the composer and moves focus to the words
optional: assist.lanes, assist.ask-now and assist.shortcut are read when the runtime is present

db.note: none directly; the engine writes requests/, conversations/ and their changes/ entries

entries.name: Mind map
entries.summary: A mind-map you make and arrange with drag and drop: a tidy tree left to right, add, edit and delete nodes, drop on a node or on a line between siblings, and a Move to menu that does every drop from the keyboard.
entries.about: A mind-map you make and arrange with drag and drop: a tidy tree from left to right, the root at the left, pills for the nodes, smooth curves for the connectors. The component holds no storage: data goes in, every user change comes out whole through onChange, and the page saves it.

config: data {nodes [{id, text, parent, order, collapsed}]}, onChange(next) with the whole next data, readOnly, label; returns {update(next), destroy()}

source.what: the pointer drag with a drop line, and a Move to menu that does the same without a drag

changed: 0.1.1: layout 'free': nodes can carry x and y and a drag drops a node, with its subtree, anywhere on the map; the default stays the tidy tree.
